item.title: Giggs Shooting Case Ends In Acquittal For Accused Lookout
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Giggs shooting trial clears an alleged scout as defense lawyers challenge phone evidence and claims about gang ties.
item.content:encoded:
Giggs was the alleged target in a London shooting case that has ended with one defendant unanimously cleared.

A jury at the Old Bailey rejected firearm, ammunition and grievous bodily harm charges against the man following a four-week trial. His barrister’s chambers announced the verdict on November 9, describing a prosecution case built around alleged scouting for the attackers.

The shooting followed the rapper’s 2025 appearance with DJ AG in Peckham, according to Garden Court Chambers. A bystander sustained a serious foot injury, while prosecutors accused the defendant of checking the area and passing information to people inside a vehicle.

The defense did not dispute that he briefly entered the vehicle. Instead, the man said he was talking innocently with his cousin and denied helping prepare an attack.

Barrister Tetevi Davi challenged the prosecution using phone records, location information and forensic material, the chambers said.

Its account also says questioning of a gang expert established that the defendant had no gang membership or association. The charges required prosecutors to prove intent to endanger life or to cause grievous bodily harm, respectively.

The injury had previously featured in a January investigation into London’s gun crime, when a detective described recovering a bullet from the bystander’s sock.

The victim’s foot bones were shattered after the bullet ricocheted, according to the officer’s account of the shooting.

Giggs has previously described years of police interference with his performances, including concerts canceled shortly before he could take the stage. In a 2024 interview, he said accusations of gang activity kept him from performing normally for roughly a decade.

The rapper recalled arranging private appearances and transporting audiences by coach, only to have authorities discover the shows.

Those restrictions were separate from the visa difficulties that delayed his first American tour, which eventually brought him to nine cities.

During that tour, Giggs spoke with AllHipHop before his Los Angeles appearance about valuing live crowds over streaming statistics. His Zero Tolerance album featured American collaborators including Jadakiss, Dave East and 21 Savage alongside Popcaan.

Linda Okoli of Titan Solicitors instructed Davi in the recently concluded firearms trial.

item.title: Akon’s “Smack That” With Eminem Earns Diamond Certification
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Akon's "Smack That" reaches Diamond status as "I Wanna Love You" and "Don't Matter" receive six-times Platinum certifications.
item.content:encoded:
Akon‘s “Smack That” collaboration with Eminem has reached Diamond status, according to the RIAA’s latest official certification records. The organization lists the Universal single at 1X Diamond, with an award date of November 13, 2026.

The same database update puts “I Wanna Love You” and “Don’t Matter” at six-times Platinum. All three songs appeared on Konvicted, Akon’s second album, which arrived in 2006.

Diamond recognizes 10 million qualifying U.S. units. The RIAA counts downloads and on-demand audio and video streams toward digital single certifications, using a conversion of 150 streams for one download. A third-party auditing firm reviews the applications and supporting figures.

“Smack That” had already made chart history during its original release. As AllHipHop reported in 2006, the song jumped from No. 95 to No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100, the biggest climb in the chart’s history at that time.

Its first week of digital sales totaled 67,000 downloads, putting it at No. 6 on the Hot Digital Songs chart. Akon discussed the pressure of following that success in an interview with AllHipHop during the album’s rollout. The rise surpassed “Breaking Free,” the Vanessa Hudgens, Zac Efron and Andrew Seeley recording that had moved from No. 86 to No. 4 earlier that year, setting the previous record.

“I just feel like as long as I’m working hard, and putting out good music, it shouldn’t be a problem,” Akon said.

Akon later described the Detroit recording sessions in a 2015 interview with The Charlatan. He said he traveled there hoping to work with Eminem and initially went to the studio late, expecting the rapper to record at night.

Instead, he discovered Eminem kept regular daytime studio hours. Akon said the two connected immediately, and that a strip-club visit the previous night helped inspire the words when he heard the track.

The song also earned Akon and Eminem a nomination for Best Rap/Sung Collaboration at the 2007 Grammy Awards. Konvicted received a Best Contemporary R&B Album nomination the following year.

“I Wanna Love You,” Akon’s collaboration with Snoop Dogg, also received a 2008 Grammy nomination for Best Rap/Sung Collaboration.

item.title: Ludacris & Organized Noize Get New Walk Of Fame Date
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Ludacris and Organized Noize move toward a February ceremony after FIFA preparations disrupted their Atlanta honors.
item.content:encoded:
Ludacris and Organized Noize have a new date for their Black Music & Entertainment Walk of Fame ceremony after the Atlanta event was postponed in June.

An organizers’ announcement dated November 13 sets the induction for February 11, 2027. Davido, Bishop Paul S. Morton, Jack the Rapper and former Atlanta Mayor Maynard H. Jackson are also listed in the class.

The announcement, distributed through outlets including The Chronicle News, places the celebration during Black History Month. Signia by Hilton Atlanta is named as the host hotel.

Ludacris’ selection had already been announced for the 2026 class, with a June 1 ceremony planned near Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The new announcement retains the honorees named for that earlier event.

In a June 10 statement, organizers said fencing associated with FIFA preparations had cut off access to portions of the Walk of Fame site. The installation prevented them from holding the ceremony as planned, although other Black Music Week events went ahead.

“The Walk of Fame monument is more than a destination,” co-founder Michael Mauldin said in that statement. He specifically named Ludacris and Jackson while promising another date for their celebration.

The Walk of Fame installs its Crown Jewel of Excellence emblems at Martin Luther King Jr. Drive and Northside Drive. Its founders are Catherine Brewton, Demmette Guidry and Mauldin, and the project involves the Black American Music Association and Black American Music Foundation.

Previous honorees include Outkast, Missy Elliott, Nas, Lil Wayne, Usher and Mary J. Blige.

Organized Noize formed in the early 1990s, bringing together Rico Wade, Ray Murray and Sleepy Brown. Their production credits include work with Outkast, Goodie Mob and TLC, including “So Fresh, So Clean” and “Waterfalls.”

Wade died in April 2024 at 52. His work included Outkast’s 1994 debut, Southernplayalisticadillacmuzik, and collaborations with Ludacris and Killer Mike. Organized Noize and the Dungeon Family issued a joint statement mourning his death.

The June postponement did not cancel the separate Black American Music Awards at Morehouse College’s Ray Charles Performing Arts Center. That event honored Jermaine Dupri, Anthony Hamilton, Kenny Lattimore and Jagged Edge.

The Black American Music Association was founded in 2017.

item.title: Michael Jai White Says He Beat Up A Rapper, But Who Was It?
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Michael Jai White’s claim that he beat up an unnamed rapper has sparked a guessing game.
item.content:encoded:
Michael Jai White has handed us all a guessing game with his claim that he once beat up a rapper, and apparently the name is going to cost us extra.

Who was it? That is the question. So far, I haven’t found a verified answer, but the story is circulating in online discussions where people are already trying to solve the mystery.

Here is the story below. Watch this and tell me what you think.

We have a claim. We have an unidentified rapper. We do not have enough information to put a face on the receiving end.

Still, you can understand why this has people curious. Usually, a rapper’s alleged fight comes with seventeen camera angles, a blurry security recording and somebody selling an interview before the swelling goes down.

I do believe this was back in the day as well. So, he did not give it a year, but it most certainly FELT like it was back in the day.

Was this somebody famous enough that the revelation would make everybody gasp? Would we recognize the name immediately? Those are questions, folks. I think it was probably a bum. I mean, there was no posse? No crew? Just a rapper all alone with MJW?

Personally, I want to know how the supposed confrontation even reached that point. What was said? What happened beforehand? Without those details, we cannot tell whether “beat up” describes a brief scuffle or something considerably more serious.

So, AllHipHop community, I’m passing this one to you.

For now, Michael Jai White has supplied the mystery. Tell me who you think it is.

item.title: Wiz Khalifa Offers Community Service In Romania As Court Weighs Cannabis Case
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Wiz Khalifa addresses Romanian judges by video, offering community service as his cannabis case heads toward a November 19 ruling.
item.content:encoded:
Wiz Khalifa offered to perform community service in Romania during a November 12 court appearance, as judges reconsider the cannabis case that once carried a nine-month prison term.

The rapper joined the Bucharest Court of Appeal by video. Digi24 reported that he acknowledged wrongdoing and expressed regret during questioning lasting about 10 to 15 minutes.

Wiz told judges he had donated to organizations opposing drug use and would continue supporting them.

The original sentencing judges had treated his celebrity status as an aggravating factor, arguing that smoking cannabis publicly could encourage young people to view illegal drug use as acceptable, rather than treating the incident as private consumption alone.

Community service has not been announced as his punishment. The judges heard him after annulling the previous prison judgment on November 3, a ruling that reopened the prosecution’s appeal rather than ending the case.

The dispute has moved between courts and produced sharply different penalties. The Constanta Tribunal initially imposed a 3,600-lei criminal fine. Prosecutors from DIICOT, Romania’s organized-crime agency, challenged that outcome and secured a prison sentence from the Constanta Court of Appeal in December 2025.

That December ruling is the one Bucharest judges have now set aside. They also canceled the warrant authorizing enforcement of the sentence, according to the November 3 order reproduced by Romania’s national news agency AGERPRES.

An earlier attempt to overturn the sentence failed in February, when the Constanta appeal court rejected his annulment challenge as inadmissible.

Wiz’s lawyers had sought to move the annulment proceedings away from Constanta. Romania’s highest court granted that request in September, sending the matter to Bucharest before the latest hearings.

The underlying charge concerns possession for personal use, not drug trafficking. Prosecutors said the rapper had 18.53 grams of cannabis and a cannabis cigarette at the Beach, Please! festival in Costinesti on July 13, 2024.

Police took him in after his onstage performance, but he was subsequently released and left Romania. Prosecutors brought the case to trial in October 2024.

The court set November 19 for “deliberation, pronouncement and drafting,” according to its short order.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Stove God Cooks Ordered To Produce Records In Babygrande’s EVEN Lawsuit
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Stove God Cooks faces a records deadline and sworn questioning as Babygrande's fight with EVEN reaches the rapper.
item.content:encoded:
Stove God Cooks must turn over subpoenaed records by November 16 and sit for a deposition in Babygrande’s federal lawsuit against EVEN. The rapper is a nonparty witness, not a defendant in the case.

U.S. District Judge Jessica G. L. Clarke granted the request from EVEN Labs and Enrique “Mag” Rodriguez in a November 9 order. She set December 1 for the deposition, while allowing Stove God and the parties to agree on another date. The location and time of the questioning will also be worked out between the rapper and the parties.

The order follows an October 21 motion seeking his compliance with a document subpoena and attendance for questioning. According to Clarke, the motion was emailed to Stove God that day, and he did not oppose it by the November 4 deadline.

The judge had warned that silence would mean the request went unopposed and would be granted.

The docket also now contains a publicly filed excerpt of Chuck Wilson’s deposition that addresses earlier claims about Stove God’s label situation. Wilson, Babygrande’s founder and CEO, gave that testimony on September 30; the redacted transcript was filed November 10.

Asked whether he had renegotiated Stove God’s agreement, Wilson denied doing so. “No, nor did I see him face to face,” Wilson testified, responding to questions about an August account of a meeting and revised deal.

The questioning then turned to whether Wilson had ever told Stove God it would cost $2.5 million to leave Babygrande. “No, all of that is false,” Wilson answered.

Wilson was also asked whether an album was coming. “An album has been on the way for five years, so yeah,” he said.

Those answers predate the Warner Records and Babygrande partnership announced November 6.

The rollout began with “Stovie’s Home (Down Down),” while All This For Me?, executive produced by Swizz Beatz, remains due in early 2027.

Babygrande’s announcement confirms its continuing music relationship with Stove God as the EVEN lawsuit proceeds. Wilson’s September testimony addressed earlier discussions, not this November deal.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: PJ Glizzy Asks For 25 Years In Prison Ahead Of Sentencing
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: PJ Glizzy's lawyer puts a 25-year request before the judge as relatives urge the court to consider life beyond prison.
item.content:encoded:
PJ Glizzy is asking a federal judge for a 25-year prison sentence, putting a specific number behind his plea for leniency in the case involving Chii WVTTz’s killing. The Bronx drill rapper’s lawyer made the request in a November 12 sentencing memorandum.

Attorney David Stern wants Judge Victor Marrero to weigh rehabilitation alongside punishment. His seven-page filing also asks the court to consider approximately two and a half years PJ Glizzy spent on Rikers Island before entering federal custody.

The request is not a sentence already imposed. Marrero accepted the rapper’s guilty plea in August after reviewing the July 29 proceeding before Magistrate Judge Katharine H. Parker.

According to Stern’s memorandum, PJ Glizzy pleaded guilty to three counts in a superseding indictment. Those charges cover conspiracy to commit murder in aid of racketeering, discharging a firearm in furtherance of a violent crime, and assault with a deadly weapon and attempted murder in aid of racketeering.

“A sentence of 25 years would mean that Paul will be released from prison when he will be approximately 45 years old. At 45 he will be a different person than he is now and will likely have learned his lesson and aged out of crime,” Stern wrote.

Federal prosecutors originally announced the case in December 2024, alleging that PJ Glizzy and others killed Chii WVTTz during a February 6, 2022, drive-by shooting in Brooklyn. The 18-year-old rapper’s death devastated his family and intensified scrutiny of New York’s drill scene.

Stern’s sentencing argument centers on what life after prison could look like for his client. He points to relatives and friends who have pledged to remain involved during incarceration and help with his eventual return home.

The lawyer describes the 25-year-old’s difficult upbringing and argues that he still has the capacity to change. His filing acknowledges the seriousness of the crimes rather than asking the judge to excuse them.

Stern also submitted letters supporting the rapper, including one from his aunt, Jenna White. Her appeal separates the crimes from the future she hopes remains possible.

White wrote, as quoted in the memorandum: “I am asking you to see him as a human being whose worst chapter does not necessarily have to be his final chapter.”

The defense says PJ Glizzy wants to earn his GED and is considering running a food truck. Those plans form part of its argument for a sentence that leaves room for a different adulthood.

Sentencing is scheduled for November 20 at 11 A.M.

item.title: Lil’ Kim’s “Crush On You” Goes Platinum During “Hard Core” Anniversary
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Lil' Kim earns a new Platinum certification for "Crush On You" as she celebrates 30 years of her debut album, "Hard Core."
item.content:encoded:
Lil’ Kim has a new Platinum certification for “Crush On You” as she marks 30 years of Hard Core. The RIAA’s official database lists the Atlantic Records single at 1X Platinum, with a certification date of November 12, 2026.

The award recognizes one million qualifying U.S. units. Under the RIAA’s digital single rules, downloads and on-demand audio and video streams contribute to that total, with 150 streams counting as one download. A third-party auditing firm reviews the applications and supporting sales and streaming figures.

“Crush On You” came from Kim’s debut album era and featured Lil’ Cease, with The Notorious B.I.G. on the chorus. Its beat samples Jeff Lorber’s “Rain Dance,” according to the Recording Academy’s retrospective on essential albums by female rappers.

The song also existed in different forms across the album and its single campaign. The Hard Core release history includes the “Crush On You” remix as a release outside the original album, alongside the remix of “Not Tonight.”

The Recording Academy’s account describes the video as a reference to The Wiz. Kim’s coordinated wigs and clothing matched the colors of the sets, while the dancers’ outfits followed the same visual scheme.

Hard Core also included “No Time” with Diddy and “Big Momma Thang” with Jay-Z and Lil’ Cease. The album reached double-Platinum status in 2001; Kim’s next two albums, The Notorious K.I.M. and La Bella Mafia, each earned Platinum certifications.

The album’s production also brought Memphis producer Carlos Broady into Kim’s circle. In a 2020 interview, Broady recalled Biggie selecting his instrumental for “Queen B####” after Diddy rejected it for Biggie’s own album.

The new single award follows another anniversary recognition in New York. As AllHipHop previously reported, the Empire State Building honored the 30th anniversary of Hard Core with a November 12 lighting tribute.

Kim is also revisiting the album onstage with Hard Core Symphony at Brooklyn’s Kings Theatre. Ticketmaster lists November 18 and November 19 performances with the Illharmonic Orchestra, both beginning at 8 p.m.

Her awards history extends beyond her solo catalog: “Lady Marmalade,” recorded with Christina Aguilera, Pink and Mya, earned her a Grammy for Best Pop Collaboration With Vocals.

item.title: Brittany Renner Responds To Courtside Outfit Backlash With A Question
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Brittany Renner responds on X after her courtside appearance with Celina Powell draws attention at the Clippers game.
item.content:encoded:
Brittany Renner responded to the backlash over her revealing courtside outfit by posing a question on X after attending the Clippers-Thunder game.

“Who wears this to a game…” Renner wrote in a November 14 post on X. Her verified account had drawn more than 641,000 views and 4,500 likes on the response by Sunday.

Renner attended the November 13 matchup at Intuit Dome with Celina Powell. The pair wore revealing black outfits, and a photograph of Renner near the courtside seats circulated alongside footage from the arena.

The picture, credited to Los Angeles Times photographer Wally Skalij, also captured spectators seated behind her. One woman appeared with her mouth open as Renner passed the row, prompting comments about the background of the photograph as well as her clothing.

The courtside outfit contrasted with her covered-up appearance at the June 2025 BET Awards, where she wore a head covering and a long dress. Renner had publicly embraced Islam before removing her hijab that month; by July 2026, she said she was no longer practicing the religion.

At the May 2, 2025, “Basketball Wives” premiere, Renner spoke publicly about embracing Islam. She told PEOPLE she had considered the faith for years before taking her Shahada, the declaration of faith.

“I felt like if I had not taken my Shahada, I was gonna go down a really dark road,” Renner told PEOPLE in that interview.

In a June 2025 interview with Bootleg Kev, Renner said she and Kevin Gates married April 6 and ended their marriage May 28. “I gave 100 percent,” Renner said. “All is well.”

She discussed that 52-day marriage and split during BET Awards weekend. REAL 92.3 LA posted the conversation June 7, 2025.

By June 18, 2025, she was posting her uncovered natural hair. TheJasmineBRAND’s contemporaneous report reproduced her Instagram caption: “I don’t have blind loyalty to any person, place, or thing.” Renner also wrote, “It’s still Alhamdulillah for everything!”

In January 2026, Hollywood Unlocked transcribed her explanation of what covering up had meant during that period. “And Islam provided that protection I needed while I was rebuilding myself,” Renner said in a “Facets Of Life With Brittany” clip.

Her later comments addressed religion directly. In July 2026, Hip-HopVibe reported that Renner said she no longer practiced Islam and wasn’t following any religion, after also undergoing a baptism. “No. I’m not in practice anymore,” Renner said when asked whether she was still Muslim, according to that report.

The Clippers beat the Thunder 113-112.

Replies under Renner’s post included a joke from @ClippPaul2X: “her first time seeing the moon up close 😭”

Another user, @jr5mics, wrote, “I had a feeling it was you.”

item.title: T-Boz’s Daughter Chase Rolison Recalls Memory Loss During Lupus Hospitalization
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: T-Boz's daughter Chase Rolison opens up about a frightening hospital stay, recovery and the work she still wants to pursue.
item.content:encoded:
T-Boz‘s daughter Chase Rolison says a lupus hospitalization last year left her struggling to remember weeks of her life and working to regain basic movement. The fashion entrepreneur described the ordeal during an interview with Reginae Carter.

Chase, whose father is Mack 10, said she initially believed the hospital stay had lasted only a few days. In the conversation on Carter’s YouTube channel, she recalled a much longer stretch and a difficult recovery.

“I like lost my memory for that whole month. I don’t even remember. I thought I was in the hospital for three days. I was in there for like 20 something days,” Chase said.

She said sitting up could take her half an hour and that she had to learn to walk again. Discussing the severity of her health struggles, Chase added, “I’ve almost lost my life three times.”

Chase credited her mother’s openness about living with sickle cell disease with helping her prepare for her own health challenges. Growing up, she accompanied T-Boz on hospital visits and watched how the TLC singer handled her condition.

T-Boz’s health has also affected TLC’s touring schedule. Last month, Chilli updated concertgoers on her recovery while continuing to perform without her.

Chase told Carter her symptoms can change from one day to the next, disrupting both plans and work. She said people who have not experienced serious health problems themselves, or known someone who has, do not always understand those limits.

“So, it’s like I can’t always go to everything I want to go to or do certain things I really want to do or like, you know what I’m saying?” Chase said.

The conversation also covered Anela Vintage, the clothing business Chase has built around late-1990s and early-2000s styles. She said its name comes from her middle name and described an appointment-based showroom in West Hollywood.

Her interest in fashion stretches back to childhood shopping trips and working on clothes with her mother. Chase said she also wants to move beyond selling vintage pieces and begin designing her own.

Chase’s longer-term goal is to open a store on Melrose.
